candidate.title: Smart-Seq/NanoCAGE/CAGEscan
candidate.scope: Assigned Illumina grouped card's template-switch cDNA schematic, with the actual drawn poly(A)/oligo(dT) material route resolved to original Smart-Seq cDNA preparation. Inventory: a separate left mRNA/Smart mechanism motif; an A-tailed 'mRNA fragment'; first-strand synthesis by MMLV RT with CCC and an oligo(dT)-linked adaptor; orange-adaptor/second-strand block; paired-strand PCR product; Purify; final DNA. Arrows connect one material route and depict no branches, mixing, cell compartments, sequencing or read-analysis step. The caption-matched upper figure on the candidate collection page specifically identifies Smart-Seq. nanoCAGE and CAGEscan remain distinct grouped title targets with paper-supported correspondence in template-switch capture, while their random-primed implementations are qualified by separate primary-supported local template-switch interfaces and method_scopes, without forcing them onto the oligo(dT)-history states. Those two local interfaces have no drawn branches or material transfer between them; they are paper-supported correspondences only. Their different eventual DNA readout carriers are explained in method_scopes, not reconstructed as complete workflows. SMART template switching is a component, not a fourth workflow. Smart-seq2, discussed alongside a separate schematic in the catalogue, and DLAF and other related-publication assays are outside this assigned image. Purified amplified cDNA is the drawn endpoint; no full Illumina adapter construction is asserted.

states.label: Purified amplified cDNA (final 'DNA' endpoint)
features: The final DNA stroke is schematic simplification after purification; no adapter-cleavage or insert-sequence transformation is depicted.
DNA is the physical carrier of RNA-derived sequence information, not the original RNA. It represents the successfully reverse-transcribed and amplified poly(A)+ RNA population.
This is the depicted cDNA preparation endpoint. The Smart-Seq paper constructs Illumina sequencing libraries from amplified cDNA in subsequent steps; the diagram does not specify that interface.

operations.label: First strand synthesis with Moloney murine leukemia virus reverse transcriptase
operations.description: The adaptor-bearing oligo(dT) primer anneals to the poly(A) tail. MMLV reverse transcriptase copies the RNA into complementary first-strand DNA and adds the terminal residues depicted as CCC, producing the RNA/cDNA hybrid shown in the first-strand panel.
operations.mechanism: Tailed oligo(dT) priming and MMLV reverse transcription; terminal transferase activity adds non-templated residues to the first-strand cDNA 3′ end. The enzyme is a catalyst, not a consumed RNA-to-DNA material endpoint.
operations.information_effect: RNA sequence is copied into a DNA carrier. Poly(A)-directed priming selects the represented RNA population and installs a primer-derived anchor at the RNA-3′-corresponding end; RNA 5′ information is retained only insofar as reverse transcription reaches it.

operations.description: In the random-primed nanoCAGE implementation identified by the primary paper, the terminal cDNA C residues pair with the template-switch oligonucleotide and reverse transcriptase copies that oligonucleotide. evidence.quote: To target non-coding, non-polyadenylated RNAs (poly-A−) and RNAs whose 3′ end has been truncated during the isolation of specific cells from the tissue of interest, we developed conditions to allow random-priming of the reverse-transcription (RT) reaction in combination with 5′ template-switching.

evidence.locator: [b00016], Results: nanoCAGE tag library carrier
evidence.quote: TS oligonucleotides and RT primers used in the nanoCAGE protocol contain EcoP15I restriction sites14 to systematically generate 25 bp fragments corresponding to the 5′ end of the template-switched captured cDNAs, thus producing nanoCAGE tag libraries (Fig. 1c).

evidence.locator: [b00017], Results: CAGEscan paired-end output and random-priming end
evidence.quote: CAGEscan was built upon nanoCAGE, but modified to accommodate paired-end sequencing for TSS determination at 5′ ends coupled with 3′ end sequencing of cDNAs at random priming sites. Rather than cleaving the cDNAs, in CAGEscan we added adapter sequences allowing for paired-end sequencing in the Illumina Genome Analyzers16 (Fig. 1d).

checks.rationale: The nonblocking unknown correctly identifies what the schematic does not select: a downstream interface from purified amplified cDNA to a sequencing-ready library. The Smart-Seq paper reports both shearing/adapter-ligation and Tn5-based construction, while the diagram ends at DNA without those annotations. This does not prevent the present amplified-cDNA architecture from being established and does not justify adding either unshown route.

evidence.locator: Rightmost arrow labelled 'Purify', from paired PCR product to simplified black line labelled 'DNA'
[b00011], Results: sequencing-library construction follows amplified cDNA preparation
evidence.quote: The amplified cDNA was used to construct standard Illumina sequencing libraries using either Covaris shearing followed by ligation of adaptors (PE) or Tn5-mediated “tagmentation” using the Nextera technology (Tn5). Both of these library preparation methods enable random shotgun sequencing of cDNAs (Supplementary Fig. 1).
